source_request: A sprint:full command that goes through all sprint phases automatically, without a human needed to initiate each sprint command or to give approvals.
source_request_verbatim: A sprint:full command that goes through all sprint phases automatically, without a human needed to initiate each sprint command or to give approvals.
interpreted_intent: Add a meta-orchestrator skill `/sprint:full` that takes a single plain-language request, chains the existing sprint phases (plan → design → execute → release-prep → retrospective) without per-command operator input, and pre-authorizes the in-flight approval gates within a clearly bounded autonomy preset. Hard ceilings from CLAUDE.md autonomy table (push to remote, paid services, production deploy, destructive migrations, secret handling) remain non-bypassable regardless of preset. The skill is composition over duplication: it shells out to scripts/sprint/{plan,design,ticket,external-service,execute,release,retrospective}.js rather than reimplementing their logic. The goal is to remove the multi-prompt keyboard cadence the operator currently has to perform when running a small/medium sprint end-to-end, while preserving every existing safety property (crash-safe checkpoints, beta consultation, ralph 3-attempt rule, routing trace coverage).
user_or_business_outcome: Operator types `/sprint:full "<request>"` once. The system writes a Plan Contract, scaffolds the requirements bundle, mints tickets, runs Ralph loops, prepares a release record, and writes a retrospective — without further keyboard input — UNLESS it hits a pre-declared halt condition (Class B/C decision outside preset, approval beyond preset's pre-authorization, Beta ESCALATE, production deploy, ESD requiring signup/billing/credentials, repeated-failure threshold). On halt, the skill writes a structured halt report and surfaces a single resume command. Day-to-day small/medium sprints complete in one invocation; risky sprints surface clearly at the right gate. Operator gets the leverage of the full sprint pipeline without the per-phase friction.

affected_surfaces.notes: New user-invocable skill body. Mode-aware (solo, adhoc; oneshot unsupported). Documents inputs, autonomy presets, halt conditions, recovery, approval gates, routing, relationship to mode.

Orchestrator script that sequences existing helpers. ~400 LOC. Phase state machine: plan → design → execute → release-prep → retro → done|halted. Persists state via existing checkpoint.js; resume via /sprint:full --sprint <SP-id> --resume. Writes a single sprint-full-report.md timeline at end.

JSON schema for the autonomy preset bundle. Fields: preset_name, pre_authorized_approval_levels[], pre_authorized_esd_categories[], stop_condition_policy{approval_required, human_setup, repeated_failure, scope_expansion, destructive, prod_deploy, beta_warning, unclear_intent}, halt_threshold_failed_tickets_pct, hard_ceilings (read-only, enumerated).

Default autonomy presets — conservative, moderate (default), aggressive. Operator-editable for their own pre-authorization. Lives in policy/ so it's discoverable next to decision-policy.md and sprint-routing.json.
Reuse via subprocess. /sprint:full constructs the payload itself (Alpha's reasoning) and shells out. Plan.js is unchanged. Verified: --payload <file> contract is stable.

Reuse. /sprint:full calls with chosen --documentation-scale (auto-derived from scope.size). Design.js writes the template scaffold; /sprint:full hand-edits the rendered files (LLM-heavy step) before minting tickets.
Reuse via subprocess for create + update. Bucket-bleed guard already requires --sprint when multiple sprints active; /sprint:full always passes --sprint explicitly.
Reuse for ESD gate. If gate fails at execute pre-flight, /sprint:full halts and writes halt report. ESDs that require signup/billing/credentials are HARD CEILINGS — never auto-bypassed.
Reuse. /sprint:full drives the Ralph loop per ticket. Stop conditions mapped to autonomy preset's stop_condition_policy. Hard ceilings remain (prod deploy never auto).
Reuse for prepare + check + report. /sprint:full NEVER calls release.js deploy. Operator does the actual deploy out-of-band. Approval auto-recorded when preset pre-authorizes; otherwise halts.
Reuse. /sprint:full invokes with --signed-off-by alpha. Synthesis is fail-open per retrospective.js contract; skeleton fallback is acceptable.
Reuse for crash-safe progress. /sprint:full writes checkpoints at every phase boundary AND every Ralph loop boundary.

Reuse for trace recording across all phases. /sprint:full inherits per-phase enforcement; no new routing logic. Single-vendor sessions get auto-recorded with allow_single_vendor=true per existing pattern.

No change. /sprint:full's writes flow through the same Edit/Write tools and are subject to the same guard. The guard's default `warn` mode during soft rollout means /sprint:full does not get blocked by routing drift.
Beta is consulted at the same gates /sprint:plan, /sprint:design, /sprint:execute, /sprint:release would consult. Adhoc mode only. ESCALATE returns are a HARD HALT regardless of preset.
Read by Beta (and by Alpha in solo). /sprint:full does not redefine decision classes — it consumes the existing A/B/C taxonomy. Class C decisions always halt.
Beta reads this. /sprint:full does not modify; current-stage informs Beta's verdicts which informs /sprint:full's halt behavior.
Add a section on /sprint:full — its place in the pipeline, when to use it vs per-phase invocation, autonomy presets, hard ceilings, halt taxonomy. Cross-link to AUTONOMY doc.

New doc explaining autonomy presets in plain English. Includes table of pre-authorized vs halted approvals per preset; enumerates hard ceilings; explains halt-report format; how operators write their own preset.
Update to introduce /sprint:full as the front door for autonomous sprints. Keep per-phase invocation documented as the manual path.

Add keys: sprintFullAutonomy (.claude/agents/00-alex/.system/policy/sprint-full-autonomy.json), sprintFullReports (.claude/project/sprint/full-reports/). Existing path-lint will catch any literal references in /sprint:full skill body — must use paths.* tokens.

May need a `full_orchestration` policy class so routing trace can record the orchestrator's own decisions (e.g., halt decisions) distinct from per-phase records. Stretch — likely not required for v0.1.

Integration test harness. Mocks plan→design→execute→release-prep→retro on a synthetic xs-scoped request. Validates halt behavior on (a) plan_quality=needs_user_clarification, (b) ESD with signup=true, (c) Beta ESCALATE, (d) approval beyond preset.

current_behavior.notes: Sprint pipeline today requires 5+ explicit operator invocations: /sprint:plan, /sprint:design, /sprint:execute (per ticket or scope), /sprint:release, /sprint:retrospective. Each command stops at gates that require operator input (approval records, ESD setup, scope decisions). Beta is consulted per-skill in adhoc mode. The pipeline is crash-safe (per-phase checkpoints + ralph state) and routing-traced (auto-recorded in each helper). But there is no single entry point that drives the pipeline autonomously. Operator can use /loop with a sequence command but that does not encode policy or halt behavior.

desired_behavior: `/sprint:full "<request>" [--autonomy moderate|conservative|aggressive] [--scope minimal_safe|recommended|expanded] [--documentation-scale auto|xs|s|m|l|xl] [--mode solo|adhoc] [--sprint <SP-id>]` executes the full sprint pipeline in a single invocation. Phase transitions are automatic. Approval gates are auto-satisfied when within the preset's pre-authorization. Beta is consulted at the same gates as today; ESCALATE halts. Hard ceilings (push to remote, paid services, production deploy, destructive migrations, secrets) are never bypassed regardless of preset. On any halt, writes a structured halt report and surfaces a single resume command. On completion, writes a full sprint-full-report.md timeline.

complexity_drivers: Composition over reimplementation — each phase's helper must be invoked correctly with the right payload/flags, and its exit codes interpreted
Approval pre-authorization needs a crisp schema so operators can extend safely without lifting hard ceilings
Halt taxonomy must be exhaustive — every existing stop condition (execute.js has 9) needs an explicit policy
Beta consultation cadence — adhoc mode requires consultations at the same gates as today; auto-mode must respect ESCALATE without burying it
Crash recovery on /sprint:full --resume must reconstruct phase state from existing checkpoints (no new persistence layer)
The skill body is LLM-heavy at the design phase (hand-editing rendered templates); autonomous mode means Alpha does that hand-edit without operator review — quality risk
Hard ceiling enforcement is policy-as-code — if pre-authorized list is misread, we accidentally auto-push or auto-deploy. Defense in depth: hardcoded enum of NEVER-bypassable ceilings inside full.js
Routing trace coverage — orchestrator must ensure every phase records its trace; release.js check refuses release without coverage

minimal_safe.summary: Chain plan → design → execute → retrospective ONLY. Skip /sprint:release entirely; operator handles release manually. Single autonomy preset (moderate). No autonomy preset config file. Hard ceilings hardcoded inside full.js. ~250 LOC orchestrator, ~150 lines of skill body, ~80 lines AUTONOMY doc. Closes the 80% case (everyday small sprints) without touching the release surface (which is where most risk lives).
tradeoffs: Operator still has to invoke /sprint:release manually — saves 4 of 5 commands, not all 5
Single preset means operator can't tune for their risk appetite — but eliminates the misconfiguration risk
No release-coverage protection in the auto flow; operator catches it when they invoke /sprint:release manually

recommended.summary: All 5 phases: plan → design → execute → release-prep → retro. Three autonomy presets (conservative/moderate/aggressive) in a config file under policy/. Operator can edit the file to extend pre-authorizations. Release phase auto-prepares the release record, runs check, records auto-approval when preset permits, but NEVER auto-deploys. Halt report + resume command on any halt. ~400 LOC orchestrator, ~250 lines of skill body, ~150 lines AUTONOMY doc + ~80 line schema + integration test harness.
tradeoffs: More surface area than minimal_safe — three presets, config schema, validation. Misconfiguration risk balanced by hardcoded hard ceilings.
Release-prep automation gives operator a one-step deploy-ready state, but adds a release.js dependency that minimal_safe avoids
Aggressive preset is opt-in via flag; not the default. Reduces 'foot-gun by default' risk.
Hits the user's stated goal: full pipeline, no per-command approval

expanded.summary: All 5 phases + (a) auto-deploy gate with explicit operator pre-authorization via a per-environment policy file (.claude/agents/00-alex/.system/policy/auto-deploy-policy.json), (b) auto-promotion of retro action_items into a new sprint plan if operator opts in, (c) per-ticket Beta consultation roll-up so the orchestrator surfaces a single decision request rather than N. ~600+ LOC, larger autonomy surface, longer review cycle.
tradeoffs: Auto-deploy explicitly violates the current 'production deploy is always operator-invoked' invariant; needs careful sandbox scoping (staging/dev only, never production)
Auto-promotion of action_items adds opinion to retrospective (currently retro is operator's analytical artifact, not an executor)
Per-ticket Beta roll-up risks burying ESCALATE in the rollup; would need careful UX
Highest leverage but highest risk; should follow the recommended scope as a v0.2 sprint

safe: Existing sprint helpers (plan.js, design.js, ticket.js, execute.js, release.js, retrospective.js, checkpoint.js, external-service.js, routing.js) have stable CLI contracts — /sprint:full will only shell out to them, not modify them
Crash-safe checkpoints already work — /sprint:full's --resume just reads paths.sprintProgress and resumes from current_phase
Bucket-bleed guard already requires explicit --sprint when multiple sprints active — /sprint:full always passes its sprint id
Routing trace recording is fail-open in every helper — /sprint:full does not need its own trace path
Beta consultation protocol is already implemented via SendMessage in adhoc mode — /sprint:full reuses, doesn't reimplement
Hard ceilings from CLAUDE.md 'Autonomy' table apply to all skill invocations including /sprint:full — no need to redefine globally
Path registry can absorb 1-2 new keys without breaking existing consumers
The 3-attempt rule in execute.js already handles repeated failure — /sprint:full just continues to next ticket when a ticket halts on repeated_failure
unsafe: Whether 'design phase hand-editing' can be done by Alpha autonomously to the same quality as operator review — the LLM-heavy hand-edit of PRD/AC/COPY/INPUTS/TRACE is the weakest link. May produce thin or wrong requirements. Mitigation: require plan_quality.confidence=high before /sprint:full proceeds; emit a warning at design phase that templates are auto-hand-edited

Whether operator's autonomy preset config file can be edited safely by Alpha (in case /sprint:full needs to record a one-time pre-authorization extension). Per CLAUDE.md, Alpha can freely edit files but this is policy; needs explicit operator action, never auto-edit

Whether the release-prep approval auto-record is safely scoped — if preset incorrectly pre-authorizes 'release_approval_required' the operator effectively loses release gate. Defense: hardcode 'release_approval_required' as NEVER auto-approvable in moderate preset (only aggressive can opt in)

Whether existing single-sprint conflict-check is sufficient when /sprint:full runs for hours — affected_surfaces may overlap with concurrent operator work. Mitigation: run conflict-check at every phase, halt+notify on warn

Whether the LLM cost of running plan synthesis + design hand-edit + N execute ralph loops + retro synthesis in one invocation is bounded — could blow the $5 ask-first threshold from CLAUDE.md. Need a cost-estimate halt gate
Whether the smart-context.js prompt pipeline degrades when /sprint:full produces N tickets worth of context within a single session — may need explicit session checkpoints
Whether the hook ecosystem (sprint-routing-guard, beta-gate, build-chain dispatch guard) plays well with the orchestrator pattern — may surface a new bypass class
needs_user_or_beta_review: Should the default autonomy preset be 'moderate' or 'conservative'? Conservative defaults are safer but reduce the user-stated goal (no per-command approvals). Moderate is the user's intent.
Should /sprint:full auto-bump the version of the orchestrator script as part of its own release? — likely no, but worth a Beta sanity check
Should the release-prep auto-approval (in aggressive preset) ever be allowed for production targets, or only staging/internal-canary? — recommend STAGING/INTERNAL only, never production
Should /sprint:full record a single decision-ledger row for the entire run, or per-phase rows? — recommend per-phase for auditability
Whether the LLM cost-estimate halt gate should be a hard halt (always halts above N) or soft halt (warn + ask once)
Whether /sprint:full should refuse to run if the current branch is `main` (to avoid accidental commits to main) — recommend yes, refuse + ask operator to switch

blocking: What is the exact list of approval levels pre-authorized in 'moderate' preset? Needs explicit enumeration in schema. Options: (a) only `none_required`, (b) `none_required` + `low_risk_design_approval`, (c) `none_required` + `low_risk_design_approval` + `medium_risk_execution_approval`. Decision must be made at design phase, not deferred.
What is the exact list of stop conditions auto-continued vs halted in 'moderate' preset? Default proposal: auto-defer on `repeated_failure`, halt on all others. Needs Beta review.
Should /sprint:full create a worktree-lane sprint by default to avoid touching main repo? Recommended: yes, opt-in via existing lane mechanism. But auto-worktree is a new behavior.
non_blocking: Should the halt report be a single .md file or per-phase logs?
Should /sprint:full emit a progress dashboard mid-run, or just final report?
Should the autonomy preset config file support per-sprint overrides, or only repo-level defaults?
Should the integration test harness run as part of /hooks:test or as its own command?

non_goals: Reimplementing plan/design/execute/release/retro logic — strict composition over duplication
Auto-deploying to production — hard ceiling, never bypassable, even in 'aggressive' preset
Auto-signing up for paid services — hard ceiling
Auto-pushing to remote — hard ceiling; orchestrator commits but never pushes
Replacing /sprint:plan as the front door — /sprint:plan stays available for operators who want explicit per-phase control
Adding new phases (e.g., 'design-review', 'qa-isolation') — scope is exactly the existing 5 phases
Adding new stop conditions to execute.js — orchestrator reuses the existing 9
Changing Beta's role — Beta is consulted at the same gates as today
Bypassing the routing-trace coverage gate at release time — coverage report must still pass
Cross-sprint orchestration (running 3 sprints in parallel from one prompt) — single-sprint only in v0.1
Building a UI for autonomy preset editing — config file is operator-editable; no UI
Auto-promoting retro action_items into a new sprint plan — operator decides what enters the next sprint
Backporting /sprint:full to v0.1 sprint installations — forward-only
requirement_areas: Orchestration state machine (phase transitions, halt conditions, resume contract)
Hard-ceiling enforcement (hardcoded, never overridable by preset)
Halt report format + resume command surface
Beta consultation cadence in adhoc mode (when, what context, ESCALATE handling)
Cost-estimate halt gate (LLM spend threshold, hard vs soft)
Crash recovery from /sprint:full --resume (reconstruct phase from sprintProgress)
Integration test coverage (4 halt scenarios + happy path)
Documentation (skill body + AUTONOMY doc + sprint-workflow update + OVERVIEW update)
high_level_story_candidates: As an operator, I can type `/sprint:full "<request>"` once and get a complete sprint pipeline run without per-phase prompts.
As an operator, I can pick an autonomy preset (conservative/moderate/aggressive) that matches my risk tolerance for this sprint.
As an operator, I can be confident that no preset can bypass the hard ceilings (push to remote, paid services, production deploy, destructive migrations, secrets).
As an operator, when /sprint:full halts mid-run I get a single resume command and a structured halt report explaining exactly which gate fired.
As Alex Beta, I am consulted at the same gates as today; my ESCALATE always halts /sprint:full regardless of preset.
As a framework maintainer, I can extend the autonomy preset config without modifying full.js code — the preset file is the policy interface.
As a sprint analyst, I can read sprint-full-report.md after a run and see exactly which phase took how long, what was skipped, what halted, and why.

preliminary_ticket_candidates.notes: request_type=feature_add with size=l and risk_level=medium. Per /sprint:plan procedure step 7, design_required=true. Tickets are minted during /sprint:design from the granular_story_candidates above. Do not pre-mint here.

external_service_dependencies.notes: No new third-party services. /sprint:full shells out to existing scripts which already use the configured LLM providers (claude/codex/gemini via dispatch-agent route per LRN-2026-04-17/04-30). Existing routing policy applies. No signup/billing/credentials needed.

approval_boundaries: Adding new policy file under .claude/agents/00-alex/.system/policy/ (sprint-full-autonomy.json) — Class A reversible file creation; no approval required for design, but operator review recommended before first use
Modifying path registry (.claude/paths.json) — Class A reversible, freely editable per CLAUDE.md

Introducing a skill that auto-records approvals — this is the centerpiece of the feature; operator MUST approve the schema for what gets auto-approved per preset BEFORE shipping. Adding this as approval gate.
Cost ceiling per autonomy run — must respect CLAUDE.md 'API calls >= $5 total: Ask first'. Orchestrator's cost-estimate halt gate is the mechanism; operator approval needed for the threshold value.
Auto-defer behavior on repeated_failure — this changes the operator-visible feedback loop. Operator should confirm 'defer + move on' is preferred over 'halt + ask'.
Branch-protection behavior — orchestrator should refuse to run when on `main` branch to avoid accidental commits to main; operator confirmation that this is the desired default.

lane.isolation_notes: Default lane is fine for this sprint (orchestrator code lives in scripts/sprint/ and .claude/commands/sprint/ which is single-owner). Worktree lane is over-engineering for this feature.

likely_founder_rejection_risks: Operator may want a simpler interface — `/sprint:auto` with no preset choice. Worth a Beta sanity check before locking in three-preset model.
Operator may reject the 'never push to remote' hard ceiling as too restrictive — they said 'no approvals' in the request. But push-to-remote is a CLAUDE.md autonomy invariant. Beta should confirm.
Operator may reject the 'never auto-deploy to production' ceiling for similar reasons. Same answer: CLAUDE.md invariant.

Operator may want /sprint:full to skip phases that are 'obviously not needed' for a tiny scope — but this is what documentation_scale already does in /sprint:design. Beta should confirm we don't need a new mechanism.
overbuild_risks: Three-preset autonomy model could grow into a full policy DSL — must stay bounded to enum + preauthorized lists, not a query language
Halt-report format could grow into a structured event log — keep it human-readable .md, single file per run
Per-phase Beta consultation roll-up risks becoming its own sub-protocol — reuse existing /agents/00-alex/beta.md SendMessage pattern
Cost-estimate halt gate is hard to estimate accurately for LLM spend — keep it coarse (token counts at phase boundaries), don't try to be precise
Integration test harness could grow into a 'sprint pipeline simulator' — keep it scoped to 4 halt scenarios + 1 happy path
missing_context_risks: Don't yet know if operator has a preferred autonomy preset semantics in mind (DSL vs enum, file vs CLI flag, per-sprint vs repo-wide). Beta should probe.

Don't yet know how operator wants to handle the design phase hand-editing — full autonomy (Alpha writes the templates) vs hybrid (Alpha drafts, operator reviews) vs explicit pause point. The user's request says 'no human approvals' but template hand-editing isn't an approval per se — it's quality production.
Don't yet know if there are other consumers of the sprint pipeline beyond this repo (downstream WarpOS installations) — /sprint:full's autonomy preset may need to be project-specific.

evidence_gaps: Exact pre-authorized approval-level enumeration per preset is not specified — needs design-phase decision documented in PRD
Cost-estimate threshold value ($5 is the CLAUDE.md ask-first line, but how does orchestrator estimate?) — needs design-phase mechanism (token count? phase count? phase-time estimate?)
Beta consultation phase context format — needs design-phase template
Integration test scenario specifics — 4 halt scenarios listed but exact fixtures/mocks not defined

resume_instructions: Sprint SP-20260518-001 has Plan Contract <PC-id>. Plan quality: needs_design (high confidence). Recommended scope: 'recommended' variant — all 5 phases, three autonomy presets, hard ceilings hardcoded, release-prep auto but never auto-deploy. Next: run /sprint:design --sprint SP-20260518-001 --documentation-scale m to scaffold PRD/HL/granular stories/COPY/INPUTS/TRACE/AC/QA/redteam/release-plan and mint tickets from granular_story_candidates. Beta should review (a) preset enumeration semantics, (b) hard-ceiling list completeness, (c) design-phase hand-edit quality risk, (d) cost-estimate halt gate threshold. If interrupted, read paths.sprintProgress#resume_command. Adhoc mode recommended for execution.
sprint_objective: Single-invocation execution of the full sprint pipeline (plan→design→execute→release-prep→retro) without per-command operator input, gated by a bounded autonomy preset that cannot bypass hard-ceiling CLAUDE.md autonomy table invariants.
